Package frc.robot.subsystems.drivetrain.module

Class ModuleSpark

java.lang.Object
frc.robot.subsystems.drivetrain.module.ModuleIO
frc.robot.subsystems.drivetrain.module.ModuleSpark
public class ModuleSpark extends ModuleIO
REV Robotics SparkMax implementation of a swerve drive module.

This concrete ModuleIO implementation uses two SparkMax brushless motors:

  • Drive motor: Rotates the wheel to control forward/backward movement
  • Turn motor: Rotates the module to control wheel direction

Encoder Setup:

  • Drive: RelativeEncoder (integrated into SparkMax) for position and velocity
  • Turn: SparkAbsoluteEncoder (separate CANcoder) for absolute wheel direction

Control Approach:

  • Drive: Velocity-mode closed-loop control via PID
  • Turn: Position-mode closed-loop control via PID

The SparkMax motor controllers run their own PID loops on-motor, with gains configured in SparkConfigConstants.Drivetrain.

Hardware monitoring:

  • Both motors registered with Alerter for fault detection
  • Connection status tracked via SparkMax error codes
  • Current draw monitored for stall/jam detection

  • Constructor Details

    • ModuleSpark

      public ModuleSpark(SwerveConstants.ModuleId id)
      Constructs a SparkMax-based swerve module. Initializes both motor controllers with their CAN IDs, attaches encoders, applies REV Spark configurations (PID gains, idle mode, limits), and registers motors with the Alerter for monitoring.
      Parameters:
      id - Module identifier containing CAN IDs and configuration for this module

  • Method Details

    • update

      public void update()
      Updates sensor readings from both motors and encoders.

      Called periodically by the Drivetrain subsystem to read current state:

      • Drive position: Integrated from relative encoder (meters)
      • Drive velocity: Current wheel speed from encoder (meters/second)
      • Turn position: Absolute direction from CANcoder (radians) minus module offset
      • Turn velocity: Current rotation rate from encoder (radians/second)
      • Connection status: REVLibError check for each motor
      • Power draw: Bus voltage and applied output scaled to actual current

      The turn position is offset-corrected because the absolute encoder's zero point may not align with the module's forward direction.

      Specified by:
      update in class ModuleIO

    • setStateSetpoint

      public void setStateSetpoint(double driveVelocity, double turnPosition)
      Sends velocity and position setpoints to motor controllers.

      Drive motor: Velocity setpoint for wheel speed (m/s → rotations/minute conversion)

      Turn motor: Position setpoint for wheel angle (radians, offset-corrected)

      The turn position is offset-corrected by adding back the module's angularOffset so the motor controller receives the actual absolute position to target.

      Specified by:
      setStateSetpoint in class ModuleIO
      Parameters:
      driveVelocity - Target drive wheel speed in meters per second
      turnPosition - Target wheel direction in radians
